newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso sees "First World inflation".
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso sees "First World inflation".

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said on Wednesday Brazil was on the way to "First World inflation" for the first time in decades thanks to government policies.

Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters Cardoso had received the latest consumer price inflation figures from Sao Paulo University's Economic Research Institute (Fipe) with "great satisfaction".
"We are heading for First World inflation of one digit," Amaral quoted the president as saying.

Fipe on Wednesday reported that consumer inflation in November dropped to 0.34 percent from 0.58 percent the month before, putting Brazil on course for what Cardoso saw as an accumulated inflation rate for 1996 of 8.9 percent.
That would be Brazil's best inflation performance since the 1950s and a stark break with the hyperinflation that hit a peak of 5,000 percent just a few years ago.

Brazil's "Plano Real" economic stabilisation plan, launched in mid-1994 when Cardoso was finance minister, identified out-of-control inflation as the chief bane of the economy. A controlled exchange rate, trade liberalisation and tight monetary policies have since curbed inflation.
"This (the inflation result) is due to the government's commitment to fight inflation without taking the country into recession," Cardoso said, according to Amaral.
